findings.area: (c) stage boundary: emission lost between B2 and B6
findings.unit_or_file: X-02 and B2-01 (01_LEDGER/units.json reference_semantics); existing edge case 'stage_subset'
findings.claim_refuted: B2-01: "段階ベクトルでは同額を B6 から差し引く（B6 と B2 の合計は変わらない）". This is false whenever B2 is outside the boundary. X-02 always forms B6 = B6-03 − B2-01 and then drops excluded stages, so the facility-management share of purchased-electricity emission ends up in no reported stage.
findings.evidence: Reference result for the study's own edge case 'stage_subset' (included stages A1-A3, A4, A5, B6): by_stage B6 = 4,013,831.9, B6-03 = 4,536,436.7, B2-01 = 522,604.8. So 11.52% of the operational-energy emission (7.3% of the reported SUM-03 = 7,121,859.6) is reported nowhere. My implementation of the written rule gives the same number, so the reference follows its definition; the definition is what is wrong. Open issue B-10 records the carve-out method but not this effect. Reproduce: repro.py, block F2.
findings.proposed_fix: Subtract B2-01 from B6 only when B2 is in the boundary, or report the carve-out as its own line. Correct the sentence in B2-01. Add a check that the included stages plus the excluded stages sum to the total of all 14 stages for every stage subset.

findings.area: (a) reference departs from its written convention: skip accounting
findings.unit_or_file: C3-01, C4-01 (behaviour observed through refcalc.registry.run_all); convention in refcalc/base.py docstring
findings.claim_refuted: base.py: "A row whose required input is missing, whose factor may not be used (licence) or whose unit cannot be converted is skipped and counted in n_skipped." In C3-01 and C4-01 a route whose factor is not licensed (or has no factor id) is dropped silently and n_skipped stays 0. In C3-01 the other routes of the same row are still added, so the row is partially computed.
findings.evidence: make_scenario(903,'W','hospital','S',60.0,dirty=True): 11 rows have a non-licensed C3 route with fraction > 0; reference C3-01 n_skipped = 0, value = 33,360.46, dropped emission 366.62 kgCO2e. The literal reading (skip and count the row) gives 33,142.09 with n_skipped = 11. make_scenario(913,'RC','residential','S',50.0,dirty=True): 19 rows with a RESTRICTED landfill factor get C4-01 by_item 0.0 and n_skipped = 0. The same units do count a missing mass (n_skipped = 1), and C2-01 and X-14 count licence skips, so the behaviour is inconsistent between sibling units. Under the literal reading my implementation disagreed on C3-01 value in 18 of 30 dirty scenarios (and downstream B4-02, X-02, SUM-02, SUM-03, SUM-07) and on C4-01 n_skipped in 8 of 30. Reproduce: repro.py, block F1.
findings.proposed_fix: Count every dropped route or row in n_skipped (or add n_routes_skipped). State in the C3-01 and C4-01 definitions whether a row with one unusable route is skipped whole or computed partially. Add a dirty-scenario test that asserts the count.

findings.area: (a)/(c) unit errors: factor units are never looked at in six units
findings.claim_refuted: base.py says a row "whose unit cannot be converted is skipped". SYS-02 says it checks "「活動量×係数」を計算するすべての組". In these units the factor's unit is ignored, and SYS-02 does not report the mismatch.
findings.evidence: On a 12-row scenario I changed only the factor unit. X-14 eol factor kg→t: value 255.3428 before and after. C3-01 route factor kg→t: 92,076.76 before and after. C2-01 haul factor tkm→kgkm: 25,673.91 before and after. A4-01 transport factor tkm→t: 68,226.27 before and after. Electricity profile set to MWh/year with grid factor per MJ: B6-03 4,536,436.74 before and after. SYS-02 ok = True in all five cases. Contrast: X-01 with factor unit 'dozen' is skipped and SYS-02 turns False. A kg/t mix-up (factor 1000) in the C stages or A4-01, or kWh/MWh in B6, therefore passes unnoticed, although the ledger's own caveats for C2-01 and A4-01 warn about exactly that. Stage tags are also only tested for A1-A3 factors: a delivery, transport or fuel factor tagged ['A1-A3'] is accepted. Reproduce: repro.py, block F3.
findings.proposed_fix: Convert the activity unit (kg, tkm, kWh) to the factor's unit in these units and skip-and-count when no conversion exists. Extend SYS-02 to these pairs and to the grid factor. Alternatively write in each definition that the unit is assumed, and reword the SYS-02 claim.

findings.area: (b)/(c) boundary event at T: rule depends on binary rounding
findings.unit_or_file: B4-01, B4-03, B5-01, B1-02 (base.py: periodic events, event_year)
findings.claim_refuted: base.py: "A periodic event with period L happens at tau = n*L ... while n*L < T (an event exactly at T is NOT counted)" (open issue B-2). With decimal inputs the event exactly at T is counted.
findings.evidence: T = 99.9 (one of the study's own NON_INTEGER_PERIODS) with period 33.3: reference B4-01 events = [33.3, 66.6, 99.89999999999999], B4-03 count = 3, B5-01 n_events = 3, B1 change years (34, 67, 100). 3 × 33.3 = 99.9 exactly, so the convention requires 2. With REBUILD_IDENTICAL the extra event is a whole rebuild of 2,541,126 kgCO2e, 10.4% of the reported SUM-03. T = 60 with period 20 correctly gives 2. Other decimal pairs that flip: (99.9, 11.1), (99.9, 16.65), (99.9, 0.3). The same rounding moves events one year late: 25 × 2.2 = 55.00000000000001 goes to year 56 instead of 55, which changes B3-01 when year 56 is a partial year (T = 55.5). In verification_population(400) every boundary-coincident life is binary-exact (27,994 cases, none counted), so the study's tests cannot see this. My float implementation agrees with the reference; an implementation in exact decimal arithmetic would not. Reproduce: repro.py, block F4.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the comparison explicitly, for example n*L < T − 1e-9·T and ceil(tau − 1e-9), or evaluate in exact decimal/rational arithmetic. State the rule in base.py and add T = 99.9 with L = 33.3 and T = 55.5 with L = 2.2 to edge_cases().

findings.area: (b) definition incomplete: time suffix of annual profile units
findings.unit_or_file: B6-02 (reference_semantics) and base.py convention "Unit conversion is a direct lookup ...; no chaining"
findings.claim_refuted: B6-02: "評価年ごとに、ガス・石油・地域熱の消費量×換算倍率×係数 を足す". The data give the consumption unit as 'm3/year', 'L/year', 'MJ/year' and the factor unit as 'm3', 'L', 'MJ'. No written rule makes these convertible.
findings.evidence: Reading 1 (literal direct lookup): no conversion 'm3/year'→'m3' exists, so all three fuels are skipped; B6-02 = 0 and n_skipped = 3. My first implementation did this and disagreed with the reference in 282 of 282 scenarios (for example B6-03 3,326,574 against 4,536,437). Reading 2 (the reference): the part after '/' is dropped before the lookup. The reference drops any suffix: gas unit 'm3/month' gives the same result as 'm3/year' (year 1: 18,220.33, n_skipped = 0), a silent factor-12 error, while 'L/year' is converted (1,911.95). Reproduce: repro.py, block F5.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the rule into base.py and into B6-02 (and B7): an annual profile unit is '<unit>/year' and only '/year' is accepted. Skip and count any other time base.

findings.area: (b) factor resolution: rules applied by the reference but not written
findings.claim_refuted: X-15: "(1) 適用条件を満たす製品固有値（EPD）、(2) 複合品なら A13-02 の複合係数、(3) 汎用係数、の順で係数を決め". The text gives a stage condition for the EPD and for composite components only, and does not say where the EPD conditions are read from.
findings.evidence: (i) A generic factor whose stages are ['A1-A3','A4'] is rejected by the reference (kind = None, A13-01 n_skipped = 1). Reading A: no stage test for generic factors, as written. Reading B: exactly ['A1-A3'], as the reference does. (ii) The EPD conditions are read from the FactorRecord only. A row whose EpdReference is expired (valid_until 2000-01-01), or declares stages ['A1-A3','A4'], or declares an unconvertible unit, is still resolved as EPD. Changing the record instead falls back to GENERIC. A disagreement between declaration and record is never detected. (iii) valid_until equal to the assessment date counts as valid; the dates are compared as strings. The synthetic data never separate these readings. Reproduce: repro.py, block F6.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the generic-factor stage rule to the X-15 and A13-01 text. State that the factor record is authoritative, or require declaration and record to agree and report a mismatch. State the '>=' date rule.

findings.area: (a)/(b) missing or unusable parts become 0.0 with no count or flag
findings.claim_refuted: base.py: "None means MISSING and is never treated as zero" and skipped rows are "counted in n_skipped".
findings.evidence: (i) Skipped rows get by_item = 0.0, the same as a computed zero; this was the only by_item disagreement with my implementation, in 30 of 30 dirty scenarios. (ii) B4-02, B3-01, B3-02, B1-02, B1-03, B1-04 and B5-01 return no n_skipped key. (iii) B4-02 adds partial renewals: with the manufacturing factor of equipment[0] not licensed, its B4-02 value goes from 11,384.15 to 109.52 (delivery, installation and disposal still counted for each replacement) with no marker. The definition does not say whether such a renewal is skipped. (iv) With a non-licensed grid scenario, B6-01 returns by_year of zeros, B2-01 returns 0.0, B6-03 falls from 4,536,437 to 1,209,863 and SUM-03 from 10,684,014 to 7,316,733; the only marker is B6-01.computed = False. (v) A missing recovery rate in B1-04 gives 0 emission, the same as 100% recovery. Reproduce: repro.py, block F9.
findings.proposed_fix: Use None for skipped by_item entries. Add n_skipped (or a partial flag) to the B-stage units and carry it into X-02 and the SUM units. State in B4-02 whether a renewal with a missing component is skipped or partially counted.

findings.claim_refuted: A13-05: "Q または w が欠損・範囲外の行は算出しない（0 にしない）". The reference checks the range of w only.
findings.evidence: Setting materials[1].quantity = −5.0 gives q_ord = −5.0, n_skipped = 0 and an A13-01 row of −15,347.11 kgCO2e, which enters A1-A3 and all sums. Reading 1: a negative Q is out of range and the row is not computed (my implementation). Reading 2: only w has a range (the reference). Related inputs without a range check: facility_management_ratio = 1.5 gives B6 = −453,424 (SUM-07 then undefined); end_of_life_recovery_rate = 1.3 gives a negative B1-04; A13-02 accepts negative mass fractions that sum to 1 although its canonical_form requires W >= 0; reconstruction_scope_fraction = 1.7 is accepted. Reproduce: repro.py, block F7; probe_b.py, probe_c.py, probe_f.py, probe_g.py.
findings.proposed_fix: State Q >= 0 in A13-05 and enforce it. Add declared ranges for the ratio inputs and skip-and-count on violation.

findings.area: (c) boundary handled inconsistently between units; undefined case that raises
findings.claim_refuted: QA-02 accepts "0 <= t < T" while B4-01 and base.py use only "0 < t < T". X-06 says "該当する段の値" but does not define the years before the first step.
findings.evidence: An explicit list [0, 30] gives QA-02 ok = True with no violations, yet B4-01 events = [30.0]; a refrigerant change list [0] produces no event. An event at t = 0 therefore passes the time check and is silently not calculated. For a STEPWISE grid scenario whose first step has from_index = 2, the reference raises TypeError (unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'NoneType' and 'float') instead of returning a result. For an unknown grid kind it silently uses the table. Reproduce: repro.py, block F8.
findings.proposed_fix: Make QA-02 reject t = 0 (0 < t < T), or document why 0 is legal and ignored. Define X-06 before the first step (error result or construction value) and validate the step list.

findings.area: (b)/(c) mass balance bound contradicts the ledger's own text
findings.unit_or_file: C-05 (units.json: reference_semantics against canonical_form and against the A13-05 caveat)
findings.claim_refuted: reference_semantics: "廃棄質量が発注質量（kg へ換算できる行のみ）を超えないこと". canonical_form of the same unit: "m_eol_i <= m_inst_i * (1 + tol)". A13-05 caveat: "解体時（C 段階）の質量は据付数量を基準にする。発注数量を使うと端材を A5-03 と C3/C4 で二重計上する".
findings.evidence: Row 0 of the probe scenario: installed 18,901.0 kg, ordered 20,984.8 kg. Setting the end-of-life mass to 19,942.9 kg (above installed, below ordered) gives C-05 ok = True with no violations. The reference follows reference_semantics (ordered mass, relative tolerance 1e-6 also applied to the mass test, which the sentence states only for the fraction sum). The check therefore cannot detect the double count that the A13-05 caveat describes. Rows not convertible to kg are unchecked: 5 of 12 here, 81 of 200 in dirty seed 903. Reproduce: repro.py, block F10.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide between ordered and installed mass and make reference_semantics, canonical_form and the caveat say the same. State the tolerance for the mass test.

findings.area: (c) design choices already listed as open issues, now quantified
findings.unit_or_file: B4-02 with B5-01 (open issue B-7); B4-02 against A4/A5 (B-11); SUM-02 with B2-01 (B-10)
findings.claim_refuted: No departure from the definitions. These are effects of definitions that are physically questionable in general terms, with their size on the study's own scenarios.
findings.evidence: (i) B-7, no reset of renewal cycles at an identical rebuild: edge case 'rebuild_within_period' (T = 60, C = 25, phi = 1.0) has B4 = 903,579 with 31 renewals; restarting the cycles at each rebuild gives 536,531 with 19 renewals. The difference is 40.6% of B4 and 1.9% of SUM-03. In 'refurbishment_divides_period', equipment[4] (life 30) is renewed in the refurbishment year 30. (ii) B-11, equipment delivery and installation are counted at every replacement but never initially, although the factors are tagged A4 and A5: in benchmark S the omitted initial amounts are 277 kgCO2e (0.12% of A4) and 3,856 kgCO2e (5.0% of A5). (iii) SUM-02 'embodied' contains B2, which is carved out of purchased-electricity emission: 1,235,572 kgCO2e, 7.0% of SUM-02 in benchmark S. Reproduce: probe_i.py and probe_j.py in the same directory.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the choices if intended, but report these sensitivities next to B-7, B-10 and B-11, and label SUM-02 as including an operational share.

checks_performed:
I wrote an independent implementation of all 35 requested units from units.json reference_semantics and the base.py docstring only. I did not open units_pre_a.py, units_b.py, units_c_sum.py or anything under fastcalc. A5-04, B7-04 and C1-01, which are outside the list, were taken from the reference as inputs to B5-01 and X-02.

Scenarios: 282 in total — 32 from edge_cases(), 220 from verification_population(220, seed 20261111, max_size='S'), and 30 with dirty=True (seeds 900–929).

Result: 1,080,781 values compared, with zero mismatches after three adaptations of my reading. The largest relative difference is 6.7e-16 (summation order in B4-02 and its sums); every other unit is bit-identical. The adaptations are reported as findings:
- B6-02: drop the '/year' suffix before the unit lookup.
- C3-01/C4-01: drop an unusable route without counting it.
- by_item: 0.0 instead of None for skipped rows.

Before those adaptations the disagreements were: B6-02 in 282 of 282 scenarios; C3-01 value in 18 of 30 dirty scenarios; C4-01 n_skipped in 8 of 30; by_item representation in 30 of 30. On clean scenarios only the B6-02 point mattered.

Values compared per unit (value, by_item, by_year, counts, flags):

- A4-01 50,925; A4-02 50,925
- B4-01 42,386; B4-03 50,361; B4-02 83,813; B3-01 18,271; B3-02 282
- B1-02 19,658; B1-03 18,271; B1-04 282; B5-01 18,553

I also ran about 150 single-input mutation probes against the reference to separate readings the population cannot distinguish: EPD source and date boundary, generic and composite factor rules, offcut and uplift ranges, refrigerant event ordering, explicit event lists, unit handling per stage, grid series kinds, stage subsets, rebuild rules, and decimal boundary events.

could_not_check:
- The reference source for the units was not read, by rule. Every statement about reference behaviour comes from run_all() results on original or mutated scenarios, so I cannot say which code line causes a behaviour.
- Units outside the list were not re-derived (A5-*, B1-01, B7-*, C1-01, STO-*, SUM-04/06/08, QA-*, SYS-*, X-03…X-13, X-16, X-17). SYS-02 and QA-02 were only observed as black boxes where they bear on a finding.
- Working data (_lines, _row_lines, _state, _multiplier) were not compared, apart from using B1-02 state in my own chain.
- Only size S scenarios were run; sizes M and L and the fastcalc unified model were not examined.
- The None-versus-0.0 and violation-path representations were normalised for the comparison; they are reported as a finding rather than counted as numeric disagreements.
- Whether any definition matches a real tool or real building data was not assessed and cannot be from synthetic data.
overall:
The claim holds for the arithmetic on valid inputs but is refuted in three specific respects on invalid or edge inputs.

**Where it holds.** An implementation written only from the definitions reproduces the reference for all 35 units: 1,080,781 values over 282 scenarios, bit-identical except for differences of at most 6.7e-16 from summation order. The time conventions (year weights, n*L < T, ceil year, year-end refrigerant changes, skipped repair year) are implemented as written and consistently across B1, B3, B4 and B5.

**Where it is refuted (reference departs from its own written conventions):**
- C3-01 and C4-01 drop routes with unusable factors without counting them in n_skipped.
- A4-01, C2-01, C3-01, C4-01, X-14 and the electricity path never look at factor units, and SYS-02 does not catch the mismatch despite claiming to check all pairs.
- A13-05 computes rows with a negative quantity.

**Where the definitions are incomplete (two careful engineers would differ):**
- B6-02 says nothing about the '/year' suffix; the literal reading gives zero fuel emission in every scenario.
- X-15 does not state the generic-factor stage rule or whether EPD conditions come from the declaration or the record.
- The "event exactly at T is not counted" rule flips for decimal inputs (T = 99.9 with period 33.3 counts a third rebuild, 10.4% of the total).

**Where a definition is wrong in general terms:**
- X-02 subtracts the B2 carve-out from B6 even when B2 is outside the boundary; in the study's own 'stage_subset' edge case 11.5% of operational-energy emission is reported nowhere.

The reference and the unified model share these definitions, so an exactness test between them cannot detect any of the above. The study's population contains only binary-exact boundary events and unit-consistent factors, so its tests do not exercise them either. I found nothing rated HIGH: no error that changes results on the clean synthetic scenarios other than the stage-subset case.
